sections.h2: Where is Katy, and which county handles my house?
sections.html:
Katy sits west of Houston and its city limits reach into Fort Bend, Harris and Waller counties, so the county that appraises and taxes your house turns on where the parcel sits. Look at your tax statement to see which county it names.

The city's demographics page gives its land area as 15.35 square miles. Fort Bend Central Appraisal District runs a parcel search and an online map where you can confirm a property, and its tax assessor-collector sends the bills for that county. For a Harris or Waller parcel, use that county's own appraisal district and tax office instead.

sections.h2: How fast has Katy grown, and how does that touch a seller?
sections.html:
Katy has grown from about 8,000 residents in 1990 to a city estimate of 28,121 for 2025. More buyers moving in has meant steady demand for houses, but also a lot of newer competing listings nearby.

The same page lists 7,490 households in a 2023 estimate, up from 4,336 in 2010. The city's own description of itself pairs old town heritage with new families and businesses, and that mix shows up in the housing stock: older homes near downtown and much newer subdivisions around them.

sections.h2: Where did Katy's older neighborhoods come from?
sections.html:
The first settlement, called Cane Island after the creek, dates to 1872, and the town site was platted in 1895 along the railroad. The first post office came in 1896, and the town rebuilt after the 1900 hurricane flattened most of its buildings.

Rice was the main crop for years, with peanuts and cotton alongside it. Katy Independent School District formed in 1918, a gas field was found in 1934, and Katy became a city in 1945. In 1986 a local committee placed historical markers on more than a dozen older homes and buildings downtown. If your house is one of those older downtown properties, ask the city planning staff what rules apply before you order exterior work.

Katy ISD serves the city, and the district campuses inside city limits are the ones buyers will ask about first.

  • Katy Elementary, Hutsell Elementary and WoodCreek Elementary
  • Katy Junior High and WoodCreek Junior High
  • Katy High School
  • Miller Career and Technology Center and the Opportunity Awareness Center

Aristoi Classical Academy, a free public charter school for kindergarten through 12th grade, also operates here. Attendance zones shift, so buyers should ask the district for the campus assigned to your address.

sections.h2: Which repairs on a Katy house call for a city permit?
sections.html:
Yes for most structural, mechanical and outdoor work. The city's Permit and Building Services division requires a permit for new construction, remodeling, roofing, heating and cooling systems, electrical and plumbing, and any job that adds or removes walls.

Pools, hot tubs, storage buildings, carports, garages, driveways, sidewalks, patios, irrigation, water heaters, demolition and house moving are on the permit list too. The city says it has adopted the 2021 International Building Codes and the 2026 National Electrical Code. Applications, plan uploads, fee payments and inspection scheduling run through an online portal, and a card payment carries a convenience fee of 3.95 percent or $3.00, whichever is greater.

Unpermitted work is a common snag at inspection. If a prior owner finished a garage or added a patio without a permit, a buyer using a loan may balk, while an investor paying cash will usually just price the risk in.

sections.h2: How do Texas property taxes affect a sale in Katy?
sections.html:
The lien dates from the first of January and the bill follows around the first of October, so the day you close decides who carries which part of the year's bill.

  • Appraisals reflect value and ownership as of January 1 (Texas Comptroller).
  • Bills are mailed about October 1, and most unpaid balances turn delinquent on February 1.
  • Protest cutoffs fall on May 15 in most years, with a 30-day alternative for late notices.
  • Homestead appraisals are capped at a ten percent yearly rise.

Fort Bend CAD offers online homestead filing and appeals by mail, office visit or online.

sections.h2: What are my choices if I need to sell fast in Katy?
sections.html:
Three routes are open to a Katy seller, and the calendar and repair budget usually pick one.

  • A listed house is seen by the most buyers, though it means open houses, a repair list and weeks of waiting.
  • Doing it yourself keeps the commission but hands you the contract work and the marketing.
  • Buyers paying cash skip the lender appraisal, so they can accept the property unrepaired and close when you say.

For a Katy house with deferred maintenance, renters still living there or an estate not yet settled, the cash route removes the repair list. Weigh every offer against what a listing would really net once commission and repairs come out.

sections.h2: How does the deed get recorded after a Katy sale?
sections.html: Deeds go to the clerk in Fort Bend, Harris or Waller County, whichever one holds the parcel. The state clerk manual wants the signature witnessed by a notary first, and it prices filing by the page with extra records charges. Title companies normally record for you, so ask for the final amount on your settlement statement.

sections.h2: What if my Katy house is headed for a tax auction?
sections.html:
When taxes go unpaid long enough, the taxing unit can sue and the property can be sold at a tax foreclosure auction, usually run by the constable or an agent hired by the unit. Texas has no single statewide list of these auctions, so watch the county clerk and county tax office sites for Fort Bend, Harris or Waller.

An owner can still buy the property back in some cases. For a homestead, farm or mineral interest, the Texas Supreme Court has described a two-year window from the date the buyer's deed is filed, with a 25 percent premium in the first year and 50 percent in the second, plus the bid, recording fee, taxes, penalties and costs. Other property gets 180 days at a premium of up to 25 percent. Any money left over after the sale belongs to the former owner, who has two years from the sale to claim it.

Should you owe back taxes here, a sale before any suit usually costs far less than letting it reach auction, because court costs and attorney fees are added to the bill along the way.

sections.h2: What should I tell a buyer about Katy's older downtown?
sections.html:
Downtown Katy still has houses from the town's early decades, and the 1986 markers on a dozen or more historic homes and buildings make a good walking tour for out-of-town buyers. Mention the history in your pitch if the house has period details, and ask city staff whether any local review applies before changing a front elevation.

The city also publishes a water conservation stage notice on its home page, and a stage 1 mild notice was posted there in August 2026. Buyers from outside the area appreciate hearing how watering is handled before they close on a lawn-heavy lot.

sections.h2: What if I owe on the mortgage or just inherited this Katy house?
sections.html:
A missed-payment spiral in Katy follows the Texas non-court route: a default letter, a short window to bring the loan current, then a posted and recorded sale notice and a first-Tuesday auction. The State Law Library walks through each stage, and a housing counselor can tell you where your loan stands.

If a relative left you the house, check whether a will exists and whether anyone opened probate. Heirs who want the homestead tax break must show the appraisal district proof of kinship and the death certificate. A lawyer in Harris, Fort Bend or Waller County can tell you which deed route fits.

faqs.q: Is Katy in Harris County or Fort Bend County?
faqs.a: Both, and Waller County as well. The city limits extend across three counties, so the county on your tax statement tells you which appraisal district and tax office apply to your house.

faqs.q: Is a roofing permit needed in Katy?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's Permit and Building Services division lists roofing among the work that needs a permit, along with remodeling and heating and cooling replacement. Apply through the city's online portal.
The city's demographics page shows a 2025 estimate of 28,121, up from 21,894 counted in 2020. The same page lists 7,490 households as a 2023 estimate.

faqs.q: By what date must a Katy owner protest the appraisal?
faqs.a: The usual cutoff is May 15 unless the notice arrived late, in which case you get 30 days from delivery. File with the appraisal district for the county where your parcel lies, such as Fort Bend CAD, which accepts filings online.

faqs.q: Will anyone buy a Katy house with unfinished repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, with a buyer who takes it as-is; a loan buyer will likely ask for repairs after the inspection. Unpermitted work is worth disclosing and sorting out early, since it can slow a loan-backed sale.
